forecaster_note: Small to fun sized surf with clean options all day — factor in the small AM and big PM high tides. NE windswell and little pulses of mid and long period S swell will keep most beaches in the chest high range. The south magnets and northerly-protected zones will be the pick, as we’re going to see some texturey N winds through the morning; breezier N’lies in the afternoon mean most breaks will see some bump, so head for south-facing shelter for the cleanest conditions. — Surfline Australia forecast team

wind.summary: N–NNW 9–20 km/h, gusting 39 — offshore at Long Reef and Curl Curl, cross-shore into Dee Why and Manly. Freshens through the afternoon.

shark.summary: Shark sighted by drone at Newport Beach 6:50am Mon 24 Aug — water was cleared. That’s the only Northern Beaches sighting in the last 24h and none at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly. SLS advise no drones flying today at Collaroy, Warriewood or Mona Vale. Feed live (latest statewide detection 18h old, 14 statewide in 24h).

days.label: Today
days.note: NE windswell at 54° is doing the work — the angle Dee Why likes, but only 124 kJ behind it and a 7s period, so sets will be sparse. Long Reef is the standout: it’s the one spot where the N–NNW breeze is straight offshore. Mid-morning on the draining tide to the 11:54am low.

dee-why.window: 9–11:30am. Tide drains off the 6:43am high to the 11:54am low — that’s when the NE windswell starts finding shape at the Point. N–NNW breeze is cross-shore here, so expect some bump on the open beach.
alerts: N–NNW breeze is cross-shore at Dee Why — Long Reef and Curl Curl get the cleaner offshore angle today

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: NE at 54° is exactly the angle Dee Why likes — but 124 kJ is modest energy, so it’ll be a short-period 7s wobble rather than a lined-up swell. Ride your high-volume board and sit deep at the Point for the frontside rights; the bay itself will feel gutless.

long-reef.window: 9am–12pm — pick of the four today. N–NNW is straight offshore here and the reef holds the 7s NE windswell better than the beaches.

tip.label: Best call of the day
tip.text: Only spot rating fair-to-good this morning. Same 124 kJ everywhere, but Long Reef converts the NE angle into 3–5ft with a clean offshore groom — go here before the 15:00 breeze builds to 20 km/h.

curl-curl.window: 8:30–11am. Offshore N–NNW cleans it up; the banks will decide it — look for the deeper corners on the draining tide.

tip.label: Backup to Long Reef
tip.text: Clean and offshore but inconsistent on 7s period — sets will be sparse. Worth a drive-by look from the headland before committing.

manly.window: Skip unless you want an easy paddle. Smallest of the four — North Steyne is cross-shore and only picking up 2–3ft off the NE.

tip.label: Low priority
tip.text: Manly filters the short-period NE angle worst of the four. Save the drive.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Short and sharp — offshore window from dawn to about 8:30/9am on a fun ENE windswell, then southerlies shut it down everywhere except Manly, which turns offshore. Set an alarm or don’t bother.

dee-why.window: Dawn to 8:30am. Hard cut-off — southerlies arrive mid-morning and it goes onshore for the rest of the day.
alerts: Wind swings S (191°, 16 km/h gusting 38) from roughly 9am — the offshore window is short

long-reef.window: 6:30–8:30am only. Best size of the four again, but it goes onshore once the S wind fills in.

curl-curl.window: Early only — clean until about 8/9am, then southerly bump.

manly.window: The one spot that improves as the day goes on — the S wind is offshore at North Steyne. Southern corner into the afternoon.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday brings a big dead-south groundswell — 8.5ft at 9s from 172° and 1116 kJ, roughly nine times today’s energy — but with a S onshore, so it’ll be size without shape and Dee Why will wrap it away. Sunday is the session: eases to 3–5ft with a light NW offshore. Plan for Sunday mid-morning.

dee-why.window: SATURDAY: big but messy — 8.5ft at 9s from 172°, 1116 kJ, S wind cross-shore. SUNDAY is the pick: drops to 2–4ft with a NW offshore at 9 km/h and rates fair-to-good. Go Sunday mid-morning.
alerts: Saturday swell is dead S at 172° — wraps badly into Dee Why, the bay will feel half the size it is at Long Reef
1116 kJ Saturday — 9x today’s energy. Serious water movement, strong rips

long-reef.window: SATURDAY: biggest of the four at 6–12ft — experienced only, S onshore at 18 km/h. SUNDAY: 3–5ft, NW offshore, fair-to-good — the weekend’s best session.

curl-curl.window: SATURDAY: 4–10ft and onshore — likely closing out. SUNDAY: 3–5ft with NW offshore, much more surfable.

manly.window: SATURDAY: the sheltered option — South Steyne / Shelly corner will be the only rideable size on that S angle. SUNDAY: 2–3ft and small.
